column3: “relatives” renders “brothers”; “our people” renders “my people,” and “she looks good to me” renders “she is right in my eyes.”
NASB reads “with his father and mother”; “came roaring toward him” renders “roaring to meet him.”
“came upon him mightily” renders “rushed upon him.”
“she looked good to Samson” renders “she was right in Samson’s eyes.”
“propound” renders “ask”; “indeed” renders the doubled verb, and “wraps” renders “linen garments.”
“something to eat” renders “food”; “in three days” renders “three days.”
“the fourth day” differs from the Hebrew “the seventh day,” following the Greek and Syriac.
“before the sun went down” renders a word read as “sun” or “bedchamber.”
“came upon him mightily” renders “rushed upon him”; “killed” renders “struck down.”
